$comment: TASK-982 §3.4.4 — the PER-RUN compiled-config `contextSchema` block, pinned across both languages. The gateway PRODUCES this block immediately before dispatch (packages/applications/src/services/workflow-exposure/effective-trigger-schema.ts::effectiveTriggerConfig, called from both dispatch paths); `interpreter.core_trigger` (apps/harness/src/harness/temporal/interpreter/nodes/core.py) CONSUMES it and validates a run payload against `contextSchema.resolved` and nothing else. Both tests/contracts/effective-trigger-config.contract.test.ts and apps/harness/src/harness/tests/unit/temporal/interpreter/test_task982_effective_trigger_config.py read this file; change it with both suites open. The invariant it locks: a PINNED trigger keeps the schema its workflow was published with, a FOLLOW-LATEST trigger carries the tenant's pin at dispatch under `effectiveVersionNumber` — and the interpreter cannot tell the two apart, because in both cases the answer is already in `resolved`. `followsLatest` is ABSENT on a pinned trigger, never `false`: compiledConfig is checksummed over its canonical JSON, so a field that always appeared would move the checksum of every artifact that never used it.

pinnedTriggerIsUnchanged.$comment: Published against v1 and pinned there. The gateway rewrites nothing, whatever the tenant has pinned since.

followsLatestCarriesTheTenantPin.$comment: Authored as follow-latest and published when the tenant was on v1; the gateway resolved the tenant's CURRENT pin (v4) into THIS run's config. `resolved` is the v4 derivation and `effectiveVersionNumber` names where it came from — both written only in a per-run config, never by the compiler.

reservedIdentityKeysAreNeverValidated.$comment: The server's own run envelope rides in `run_payload` beside the authored context. `_authored_context` strips it before the check, so a closed schema stays exactly as sharp as its author meant it while the platform's own keys pass — the TASK-930 D-2 rule, restated here because a per-run rewrite must not change it.
